div.head: III Eg 1.1
div.ab: Þæt is þonne, þæt ic wille, ðæt ælc man sy folcrihtes wyrðe, ge earm ge eadig, ⁊ him man rihte domas déme.
Þæt is þonne ærest, þæt ic wille, þæt ælc man sy folcrihtes wyrþe, ge earm ge eadig, ⁊ him man rihte domas deme.
Uolo, ut omnis homo sit dignus iuris publici, pauper et diues, quicunque sit, et eis iusta iudicia iudicentur.
Þæt is þonne ærest þæt ic wille, þæt ælc man sy folcrihtes wurðe, ge earm ge éadig, ⁊ heom man rihte domas deme.
Þæt is þonne ærest: þæt ic wille ðæt ælc man sy folcrihtes wyrðe, ge earm ge eadig, and him man rihte domas deme.
In the first place, my will is that every man, rich or poor, obtain the benefit of the public law and be awarded just decisions.
This is foremost: I command that every person, rich or poor, be granted their rights under civil law and granted just judgments.
Namely, then, that it is my will that every man, whether poor or rich, is to be entitled to the benefit of the common law, and just judgments are to be judged for him.
Nämlich erstens nun, dass ich will, dass jedermann, so arm wie reich, Volksrechtes theilhaftig sei, und ihm gerechte Urtheile ertheilt werden.
Namely, first, that I will that everyone, poor as well as rich, be entitled to folk-right, and that just judgments be given him.
div.note: Vgl. II Ew. 8 I Ew. Pr.
‘ærest’ should be supplied in G from A, D and II Cn 1. Liebermann compares II Ew 8; I Ew Pr.
